package_info.package_manager: Windows (malware distributed via USB, RAR, DLL side-loading)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects Windows 10 up to build 22621, exploits CVE-2023-36802 and CVE-2023-29360)
package_info.why_malicious: Raspberry Robin is a worm that spreads via USB drives and network shares, downloads and executes additional malware, exploits Windows vulnerabilities for privilege escalation, and employs advanced evasion and persistence techniques. It is used for initial access, data theft, espionage, and as a loader for other malware.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user opens malicious RAR file and executes OleView.exe)
execution_context.file_location: File.Chapter-1.rar (RAR archive downloaded from Discord, contains malicious DLL)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious DLL side-loaded by OleView.exe, executed when user opens the RAR and runs the executable.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code is loaded by OleView.exe via DLL side-loading, executes payload in the context of a trusted process, and establishes persistence or downloads further malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DLL side-loading via a legitimate Microsoft-signed executable is a common malware evasion technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal DLLs loaded by OleView.exe should be legitimate and not contain malicious payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software may use DLLs for extending functionality, but not for executing hidden payloads.
key_indicators: DLL side-loading by a trusted Microsoft binary
Execution of code not present in the original application

execution_context.trigger: runtime (privilege escalation phase after initial code execution)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into cleanmgr.exe (Windows Disk Cleanup utility) via KernelCallbackTable injection

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: KernelCallbackTable injection technique used to inject exploit code into cleanmgr.exe, which then loads an external PE containing the CVE-2023-36802 exploit.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects a kernel exploit into cleanmgr.exe using KernelCallbackTable injection, loads an external PE in memory, and exploits CVE-2023-36802 to escalate privileges to SYSTEM.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: KernelCallbackTable injection is a sophisticated and rarely legitimate technique, especially when used to load privilege escalation exploits.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software should not inject code into system utilities or exploit kernel vulnerabilities.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security tools may use process injection for monitoring, but not for privilege escalation.
key_indicators: Exploitation of kernel vulnerabilities for SYSTEM privileges

execution_context.file_location: Malicious loader in memory (not written to disk)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Loader code that adapts exploit offsets based on Windows version, obtains EPROCESS addresses via NtQuerySystemInformation and SYSTEM_HANDLE structures, and creates random pipe names with UuidCreate and UuidToStringW.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the loader adapts exploit parameters to the victim's Windows version, locates kernel structures, and prepares for privilege escalation by generating unique pipe names.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dynamic adaptation to OS version and direct kernel structure manipulation are hallmarks of advanced malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not query kernel structures or adapt exploit code based on OS internals.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing tools may use similar techniques in controlled environments.
key_indicators: Use of NtQuerySystemInformation for kernel structure discovery

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Evasion code that detects virtual machines and sandboxes, alters behavior or terminates if analysis environment is detected.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks for virtual machine artifacts and analysis environments, and evades detection by altering execution or terminating.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Anti-VM and anti-analysis checks are common in malware to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not attempt to detect or evade virtual machines.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some DRM or licensing software may check for VMs, but not to evade malware analysis.

attack_chain.action: User downloads malicious RAR archive (File.Chapter-1.rar) from Discord and extracts it.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious DLL is side-loaded by OleView.exe.

attack_chain.action: OleView.exe side-loads the malicious DLL, which executes initial payload and establishes persistence or downloads further malware.
Malware injects exploit code into cleanmgr.exe using KernelCallbackTable injection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Loader prepares and executes kernel exploit.

attack_chain.action: Loader adapts exploit to victim's Windows version, locates kernel structures, and generates unique pipe names.
Exploit code abuses CVE-2023-36802 (or CVE-2023-29360) to escalate privileges to SYSTEM.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware achieves SYSTEM privileges and can deploy additional payloads.

attack_chain.action: Malware performs anti-VM and anti-analysis checks to evade detection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Continued persistence and further malicious activity.

behavioral_signatures: DLL side-loading by OleView.exe or other Microsoft-signed binaries
Process injection into cleanmgr.exe or other system utilities
In-memory only loaders and exploit code (no disk artifacts)
Dynamic querying of kernel structures (NtQuerySystemInformation, SYSTEM_HANDLE)
file_indicators: RAR archives named File.Chapter-1.rar or similar
network_indicators: RAR archives downloaded from Discord CDN
Potential C2 or payload download activity following DLL execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for DLL side-loading activity, especially involving OleView.exe and unexpected DLLs. Detect process injection into system utilities like cleanmgr.exe. Look for in-memory only loaders and exploit code that adapts to OS version. Flag use of NtQuerySystemInformation for kernel structure discovery by non-system processes. Watch for anti-VM and anti-analysis routines. Correlate RAR archive downloads from Discord with subsequent suspicious process activity.
